title: Childhood type 1 diabetes: an environment-wide association study across England.
ehr_evidence: We obtained type 1 diabetes data from National Health Service (NHS) Digital hospital episode statistics (HES) records held by the UK Small Area Health Statistics Unit.
summary: An ecological environment-wide association study using national HES data assessed associations between 53 demographic and environmental factors and incident childhood type 1 diabetes incidence in 13,948 children aged 0-9 years across 354 local authority districts in England (2000-2011).
key_findings: Overall type 1 diabetes incidence was 21.2 (95% CI 20.9, 21.6) per 100,000 children aged 0-9 years.

30 of 53 environmental/demographic variables were significantly associated with type 1 diabetes after Bonferroni correction (p < 0.0009), with 15 remaining significant after accounting for spatial dependency in Bayesian disease mapping.
Air pollutants (PM10, PM2.5, nitrogen dioxide, nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide) were all inversely associated with type 1 diabetes incidence.

Multivariable ecological regression retained significant associations for the IMD living environment domain (RR 0.995; 95% CrI 0.991, 0.998) and radon potential class (RR 1.044; 95% CrI 1.015, 1.074).
Radon potential class showed a consistent, significant positive association with type 1 diabetes risk across all analyses.
No significant association was found for meteorological variables (sunshine duration, temperature, ultraviolet radiation), nitrates in drinking water, land use, or pesticide use.
captured_features: Land cover (green, blue, built-up, intense agriculture)
PM10, PM2.5, nitrogen dioxide, nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, ozone, benzene
Index of Multiple Deprivation and domains
Case counts and age/sex-adjusted expected counts by local authority district
study_design: Ecological environment-wide association study (EnWAS) with Bayesian disease mapping and multivariable ecological (Poisson) regression at local authority district level
population: 13,948 children aged 0-9 years with incident type 1 diabetes in England (2000-2011), aggregated to 354 local authority districts
exposure_domain: Broad environmental and demographic exposome (air pollution, meteorological factors, land use, soil metals, water nitrates, pesticides, night-time light, socioeconomic deprivation, ethnicity)
limitations: Ecological (area-level) design means associations may not reflect individual-level relationships (ecological bias).
High intercorrelation among variables prevented a full mutually-adjusted model, leaving potential confounding by measured and unmeasured factors (e.g. diet, family history).
Exposure variables were aggregated to LAD level, losing spatial granularity and potentially attenuating associations.
Temporal mismatch between environmental and health data collection periods.
HES dataset may include readmissions/prevalent cases and miss children treated outside the NHS.
No individual-level data on family history, lifestyle, or diet available.
data_availability_statement: The majority of the demographic and environmental factors included in the study were derived from Crown copyright data and are available via the links provided in the text and references. HES data are available via NHS Digital on application with appropriate ethics and governance permissions; we do not hold data provider, ethics or governance permissions to share these health data with third parties.
